builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: WordInferBench: Can Agents Infer How to Edit from Word Document Context?
summary: This benchmark replaces fully specified document-editing instructions with 280 base instances evaluated under descriptive, referential, and inferential conditions across 13 object types and 81 attributes. It costs access to capable coding-agent systems and an evaluation setup rather than training or dedicated infrastructure, and it adds benchmark complexity without by itself improving production editing quality. It can fail to transfer if its Common Crawl-derived Word documents, exemplar-recoverable formatting assumptions, or agent harness do not match the reader's production documents and workflows.
rationale: It is useful for assessing whether an agent can infer formatting edits from document context, but for a constrained production team it is primarily an evaluation reference rather than an immediately deployable technique.

claims.statement: This benchmark replaces fully specified document-editing instructions with 280 base instances evaluated under descriptive, referential, and inferential conditions across 13 object types and 81 attributes. It costs access to capable coding-agent systems and an evaluation setup rather than training or dedicated infrastructure, and it adds benchmark complexity without by itself improving production editing quality. It can fail to transfer if its Common Crawl-derived Word documents, exemplar-recoverable formatting assumptions, or agent harness do not match the reader's production documents and workflows.
The best-performing evaluated system, Claude Code with Opus 4.6, achieves a 62.9% task-level pass rate on descriptive variants but only 40.7% on inferential variants.
